subjects.name: Agriculture & Nutrition
mcq: Growing trees with crops or livestock on the same land
Agroforestry integrates trees with agricultural production.
Which is a benefit of agroforestry?
Tree roots help hold soil and reduce erosion.
Which is a planting material for establishing trees?
Seeds can be used to establish trees.
Which structure helps conserve surface runoff?
Terraces slow runoff and encourage infiltration.
Physical condition of soil for plant growth
Tilth describes soil condition, especially suitability for cultivation.
Which is a category of soil tilth?
Fine tilth is one category used in seedbed preparation.
Which is a vegetative planting material?
Stem cuttings are vegetative planting materials.
Which is a method of planting crops?
Broadcasting is a crop planting method.
Which factor can help predict planting time?
Weather information helps farmers plan planting.
Home Science education helps learners to:
Home Science develops practical home-management skills.
Which is a safe practice when roasting food?
Keep food at a safe distance from flames
Touch hot metal with bare hands
Safe distance reduces burns and fire risks.
When buying household goods, one should consider:
Quality and price are important considerations.
Using it again for another suitable purpose
Reuse extends the useful life of an item.
Processing used materials into new products
Recycling converts waste materials into usable products.
A deficiency disease may result from:
Nutrient deficiencies can cause deficiency diseases.
Making or adapting alternatives when standard tools are unavailable
Which is a household goods sales outlet?
Which action can help save income when shopping?
Which is a challenge when buying household goods?
Changing prices can make budgeting difficult.
structured: Define agroforestry.
The practice of deliberately growing trees or shrubs together with crops and/or livestock on the same land. (2)
State four environmental benefits of agroforestry trees.
Reduce soil erosion, provide shade, improve biodiversity, act as windbreaks, add organic matter, conserve water/carbon. Any four.
Name three planting materials used to establish agroforestry trees.
Seeds, seedlings, stem cuttings, root suckers or other suitable vegetative materials. Any three.
Name three structures used to conserve surface runoff.
Terraces, contour bunds, water-retention pits, infiltration ditches, check dams. Any three.
State four practices used when caring for established agroforestry trees.
Watering, mulching, weeding, pruning, protecting from livestock/pests, applying manure. Any four.
Give four sites where crops may be planted.
Seedbeds, fields/gardens, containers, raised beds, ridges or planting holes. Any four appropriate sites.
Define soil tilth.
The physical condition or state of soil in relation to its suitability for cultivation and plant growth. (2)
Name three categories of soil tilth according to planting material size.
Fine, medium and coarse tilth. (1 each)
Describe three steps in preparing a ground seedbed.
Clear vegetation/debris; dig or loosen soil; break clods and level/rake to a suitable tilth. (1 each)
Give two main categories of planting materials.
Sexual materials (seeds) and vegetative/asexual materials. (1 each)
Name three vegetative planting materials.
Stem cuttings, root cuttings, suckers, tubers, bulbs, rhizomes. Any three.
State three methods of planting crops.
Broadcasting, drilling/row planting, dibbling, transplanting. Any three.
Give one way of predicting the time of planting.
Use weather forecasts/seasonal rainfall information or observe reliable local rainfall patterns. (2)
State two factors that determine time of planting.
Onset and reliability of rains, soil moisture, crop type, temperature, availability of water or market timing. Any two explained.
State four roles of Home Science education.
Promotes healthy living, food/nutrition knowledge, home management, budgeting/resource use, hygiene and safety, family relationships. Any four.
Give three guidelines for cooking food by roasting.
Prepare food appropriately; use moderate, even heat; turn food as needed; cook thoroughly; avoid charring. Any three.
State three safety measures when roasting food.
Use suitable tools/oven mitts; keep flammable items away; supervise fire/heat; use stable equipment; avoid touching hot surfaces. Any three.
State four factors to consider when buying household goods and services.
Price, quality, durability, need, safety, quantity, warranty, availability and seller reliability. Any four.
Differentiate between reusing and recycling and give one example of each.
Reuse means using an item again without major processing (1), e.g. jar as storage (1); recycling processes waste into new material/product (1), e.g. paper into new paper (1).
Explain two reasons for improvising food-preparation equipment.
Makes cooking possible when standard equipment is unavailable; reduces cost; encourages creativity and resource use. Any two explained.
Name four outlets where household goods and services may be obtained.
Supermarkets, shops, markets, wholesalers, online stores, cooperatives. Any four.
State four methods of buying household goods and services.
Cash purchase, hire purchase, credit, lay-by, online purchase, instalment payment. Any four.
Give five ways of saving income when buying household goods.
Prepare a budget, compare prices, buy only needed items, use shopping lists, buy durable goods, avoid impulse buying, take advantage of genuine discounts. Any five.
State five challenges people may face when buying household goods and services.
High prices, counterfeit goods, poor quality, shortages, misleading advertising, transport costs, price changes, limited access. Any five.
State three properties of cotton fibre.
Soft, absorbent, breathable, comfortable, washable and strong when wet. Any three.

source.basis: Water conservation, agroforestry, runoff structures, soil tilth, seedbeds, planting materials/methods/time, weeds, Home Science, roasting, consumer choices, reuse/recycling, nutrition, household goods, saving and cotton fibres. Supplementary JSLH practice included.

mcq: Which is an example of a 3D artwork?
A colour wheel is used to:
Which are the primary colours in the traditional pigment colour model?
Traditional primary pigment colours are red, yellow and blue.
Analogous colours are neighbours on the colour wheel.
The three basic properties of colour include hue, value and:
Intensity is the third common colour property.
Adding white to a colour produces a:
A tint is made by adding white.
Adding black to a colour produces a:
A shade is made by adding black.
Perspective in art helps create an impression of:
Perspective represents depth on a flat surface.
Red and yellow combine to make orange.
A pass in netball used to move the ball over a short distance is often a:
A chest pass is a common short accurate pass.
How many players from each team are on court in netball?
A standard netball team has seven players on court.
A netball player must pass or shoot within:
The standard indoor handball court is 20 by 40 metres.
A handball penalty throw is taken from the:
The penalty throw is taken from the 7-metre line.
A drum is struck to produce sound.
A guitar produces sound when its strings:
A soloist is a performer who:
Sings or performs a solo part
A soloist performs alone or leads a solo section.
structured: Define a 3D art form and give three examples.
A form with length, width and height (1); examples such as sculpture, pottery, carving, modelling. Any three (1 each).
Define still-life drawing.
A drawing of arranged non-living objects, such as fruits, utensils or bottles. (2)
Explain the meaning of composition in visual art.
The arrangement of visual elements in an artwork to create an organised and balanced whole. (2)
Define painting and name three tools/materials used.
Applying pigment/paint to a surface to create an image (2); brush, paint, palette, paper/canvas, water. Any three (1 each).
What is a colour wheel?
A circular arrangement of colours showing relationships among primary, secondary and related colours. (2)
Name the three primary colours in the traditional pigment model.
Red, yellow and blue. (1 each)
Give three pairs of analogous colours.
Red/orange, yellow/orange, yellow/green, blue/green, blue/violet, red/violet. Any three adjacent pairs.
Name the three basic properties of colour.
Hue, value and intensity/saturation. (1 each)
Define perspective in drawing.
A technique for representing three-dimensional depth and distance on a two-dimensional surface. (2)
Name three components or elements used when constructing perspective.
Horizon line, vanishing point and orthogonal/receding lines. (1 each)
Explain tint and shade.
Tint is made by adding white to a colour; shade is made by adding black. (1 each)
Describe how to create an intensity scale using orange paint.

Mix red and yellow to make orange; progressively alter the mixture with its complement/neutralising colour or controlled pigment addition to show stronger to duller intensity. Award for safe, logical graduated procedure. (3)
Explain how to make a colour gradation strip from red to yellow.
Prepare red and yellow; mix successive proportions in steps; paint adjacent bands showing gradual transition through orange. (3)
Define passing and reception in ball games.
Passing is sending the ball to a teammate (1); reception is receiving/controlling a ball from another player (1).
Define pivoting and marking in games.
Pivoting is turning on a planted foot while maintaining control (1); marking is guarding/opposing a player to limit their movement or options (1).
Name two types of passes used in handball.
Overarm/shoulder pass, bounce pass, chest pass, wrist pass. Any two.
State the dimensions of a standard handball court.
From what distance is a handball penalty throw taken?
7 metres from the goal. (1)
State two landing techniques used in netball footwork.
One-foot landing and two-foot landing. (1 each)
How many players from each team play on a netball court?
Seven players. (1)
State the time limit for a netball player to pass or shoot after receiving the ball.
Three seconds. (1)
Give four ways dancers can remain safe during a performance.
Warm up, clear the stage, wear suitable footwear/costume, check props, follow instructions, avoid unsafe lifts. Any four.
Name two activities dancers should do before a stage performance.
Warm-up/stretching and rehearsal; checking costume/props or stage positions also acceptable. Any two.
Name two materials used to make a sisal skirt.
Sisal fibre and string/thread; suitable waistband or binding material also accepted. (1 each)
Explain how a whistle and a guitar produce sound.
Whistle: blown air vibrates (1); guitar: plucked/strummed strings vibrate (1).

source.basis: 3D forms, still-life, composition, painting, colour wheel, primary/analogous colours, colour properties, perspective, tints/shades/intensity/gradation, netball, handball, footwork, dance safety, performance and sound production.

subjects.name: CRE
mcq: Which statement is a similarity between the biblical creation account and many African creation stories?
A supreme creator is responsible for the origin of life
The world made itself without any cause
Both traditions commonly describe a supreme creator as the source of creation.
According to Genesis 1, what did God create on the first day?
Genesis 1 describes the creation of light on the first day.
What was created on the second day in the first biblical creation account?
The second day describes the expanse separating waters.
Which creation work is associated with the third day in Genesis 1?
The third day describes dry land, seas and plants.
What was created on the fourth day according to Genesis 1?
The heavenly lights are appointed on the fourth day.
Which creatures were created on the fifth day in Genesis 1?
The fifth day includes creatures of the waters and birds.
Which creation work is associated with the sixth day?
Genesis 1 places land animals and human beings on the sixth day.
What did God do on the seventh day in the first creation account?
The seventh day is described as a day of rest and blessing.
Which book contains the two biblical creation accounts studied in Grade 7 CRE?
The creation accounts are found in Genesis.
Which reference gives the second biblical creation account in the source paper?
The supplied assessment specifically identifies Genesis 2:4–25.
In Genesis 2, what was formed from the dust of the ground?
Genesis 2 describes God forming the man from the dust of the ground.
According to Genesis 2, what did God do after forming the man from dust?
Breathed into his nostrils the breath of life
Sent him to build a city
The account says God breathed the breath of life into the man.
What was the name of the garden where God placed the man in Genesis 2?
What was the man instructed to do in the Garden of Eden?
Work it and take care of it
The man was placed in the garden to work it and care for it.
What was created as a companion for the man in Genesis 2?
The account describes the creation of the woman as a companion.
Which attribute of God is shown by creation of the world?
Which attribute of God is reflected in providing plants and food for living things?
Providing for living things reflects care and provision.
Which statement best expresses the Christian belief that God is eternal?
God has no beginning or end
Eternal means without beginning or end.
Why do Christians care for animals, fish and birds?
They are part of God's creation and should be treated responsibly
They should all be kept as pets
They are only useful for entertainment
Christians understand living creatures as part of God's creation and a trust to care for.
Which action shows care for birds?
Providing safe nesting places and protecting habitats
Protecting habitats and nests helps birds survive.
Avoiding pollution of rivers and lakes
Clean water is essential for aquatic life.
Providing clean water, food and shelter
Responsible care includes food, water, shelter and humane treatment.
Which is a likely effect of misusing natural resources?
Misuse can damage land and ecosystems, including through soil erosion.
How can cutting trees carelessly affect the environment?
It can cause soil erosion and loss of habitats
Tree removal can expose soil and destroy habitats.
Which action is an example of sustainable use of natural resources?
Planting trees to replace those cut down
Replanting trees helps maintain resources for future generations.
Which is an appropriate use of the Bible during worship?
Reading passages and guiding prayers or teaching
Replacing all school books with it
The Bible is read and used for teaching and worship.
How may the Bible be used during a Christian wedding?
Scripture may be read to guide and bless the marriage ceremony.
How can the Bible be used when visiting a sick person?
Reading encouraging passages and offering comfort
Bible passages may provide spiritual encouragement and comfort.
How many books are in the Protestant Old Testament?
The Protestant Old Testament contains 39 books.
How many books are in the Protestant New Testament?
How many books are in the Protestant Bible altogether?
The Protestant Bible has 39 Old Testament and 27 New Testament books.
Which of the following is one of the major prophets?
Isaiah is traditionally grouped among the major prophets.
Which list contains books traditionally associated with the major prophets?
Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel and Daniel
Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy
Matthew, Mark, Luke, John and Acts
Ruth, Esther, Job, Psalms and Proverbs
The five books traditionally grouped in this category are Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel and Daniel.
Which life skill helps people understand another person's feelings?
Empathy is the ability to understand and share another person's feelings.
Which life skill helps people settle disagreements peacefully?
Conflict-resolution skills help people address disagreements constructively.
Which behaviour shows effective communication in a friendship?
Respectful listening and speaking support healthy relationships.
Which is a commonly abused drug in Kenya?
Alcohol is among substances that may be misused or abused.
Which is a possible reason some young people begin abusing drugs?
Peer pressure can influence young people to experiment with drugs.
Which is a possible consequence of drug abuse?
Drug abuse can lead to dependence and physical, mental and social harm.
Which is a safe response to an online stranger asking for a home address?
Do not share it; tell a trusted adult
Personal information should not be shared with unknown people online.
Which action is an example of cyberbullying?
Repeatedly sending hurtful or threatening messages
Cyberbullying involves using digital communication to harm or intimidate others.
What should a learner do before sharing another person's photograph online?
Respecting consent and privacy is important when sharing images.
Which is a responsible use of social media?
Sharing accurate, respectful and appropriate content
Responsible use protects others and avoids misinformation or harm.
Which creation account in Genesis presents creation in a sequence of days?
The second account in Genesis 2 only
Genesis 1 presents creation in a sequence of days.
Which day in Genesis 1 is associated with the creation of the sun, moon and stars?
The fourth day describes the heavenly lights.
What is the meaning of stewardship in relation to creation?
Responsible care and management of what has been entrusted to people
Stewardship means caring responsibly for resources and creation.
Which of the following best demonstrates stewardship of forests?
Replanting trees and preventing illegal clearing
Replanting and protecting forests support sustainable use.
Which action is most likely to conserve water at home?
Washing paths with a hose for long periods
Repairing leaks reduces unnecessary water loss.
Which is a positive way to respond to a disagreement with a friend?
Listen and discuss the issue calmly
Which life skill helps a learner make a choice after considering possible outcomes?
Decision-making involves considering options and consequences.
Which value is shown when a learner admits making a mistake?
Choosing not to seek revenge after an apology
Forgiveness allows people to move beyond wrongdoing without revenge.
Which of these is an example of a major prophet book?
Ezekiel is traditionally included among the major prophet books.
The four Gospels are in the New Testament.
Which testament includes the books of Genesis and Exodus?
Genesis and Exodus are books of the Old Testament.
Which is an appropriate occasion for reading the Bible with a family?
A sports injury treatment instead of first aid
Families may read the Bible during devotion and discussion.
Which action shows respect for a person of a different Christian denomination?
Respectful coexistence allows differences without hostility.
Which is an example of social media misuse?
Sharing a classmate's private photograph to embarrass them
Sharing a school announcement with permission
Sharing private images to humiliate someone violates privacy and can be cyberbullying.
Why should a learner avoid sharing passwords with online friends?
The account could be accessed or misused
Passwords protect accounts and must remain confidential.
Which is the safest response to an invitation from an online stranger to meet secretly?
Decline and tell a trusted adult
Secret meetings with unknown people can put a child at risk.
Which substance is a stimulant commonly referred to as miraa or khat?
Khat is a stimulant plant that can be misused.
Which of the following is a possible social effect of drug abuse?
Drug misuse can strain relationships and create conflict.
What is one reason the Bible is important to Christians?
It provides teaching and guidance for faith and conduct
It is used only for decoration
Christians use the Bible as a source of faith, teaching and guidance.
Which of these is a moral value taught in CRE?
Compassion involves caring about the suffering and needs of others.
Which statement about the second creation account is supported by Genesis 2?
The man was placed in a garden to work and care for it
The sun and moon were created on day four
The sea creatures were created on day five
The seventh day was blessed after six days
Genesis 2 describes the man being placed in Eden to work and care for it.
What does the creation of the woman in Genesis 2 communicate in the account?
That people should live without others
That animals are not part of creation
The account presents the woman as a companion for the man.
Which is a responsible response to seeing an animal being mistreated?
Seek safe help from an adult or relevant authority
Record it for entertainment and share it
A safe report helps protect the animal without escalating danger.
Which human activity is most likely to destroy fish habitats?
Planting trees near a river carefully
Chemical pollution damages aquatic habitats and organisms.
Which is a likely result of overgrazing?
Loss of vegetation and soil erosion
Overgrazing removes plant cover and exposes soil to erosion.
Which action helps reduce air pollution?
Why should Christians avoid wasting food and water?
Resources should be used responsibly and others may need them
It has no effect on people
Responsible use reflects care for resources and concern for others.
Which skill enables a learner to express a need firmly while respecting others?
Assertiveness communicates needs clearly without violating others' rights.
Which of the following helps build trust in a friendship?
Keeping promises supports reliability and trust.
Which action should a learner take after receiving a threatening online message?
Save evidence, block/report the sender and tell a trusted adult
Share it publicly with personal details
Arrange to confront the sender alone
Reporting to trusted adults and platform tools helps protect the learner.
Which of the following is a safe social media privacy practice?
Limit profile details visible to strangers
Privacy settings reduce exposure of personal information.
Which is an example of a positive use of social media for learning?
Social media can support learning when used responsibly and with guidance.
Which of the following is a New Testament Gospel?
Luke is one of the four Gospels in the New Testament.
Which prophet is associated with the book of Daniel?
Daniel is traditionally associated with the book bearing his name.
Which phrase best describes the nature of God as creator?
God depends on human beings to create the universe
God is one of the created animals
God has no concern for creation
The Genesis accounts present God as the creator.
What is one way to show respect for the Bible during a worship service?
Handle it carefully and listen respectfully to readings
Use its pages as scrap paper
Respectful handling and attention reflect its significance in worship.
structured: State five similarities between the biblical creation account and African creation stories.

Award 1 mark each for relevant similarities supported by taught examples, such as belief in a supreme creator; creation of the world and living things; human beings having a special place; creation being purposeful; people receiving responsibility to care for creation.
Explain five ways Christians can protect and care for animals, fish and birds.
Award 1 mark each: provide food/water/shelter; protect habitats; avoid cruelty; prevent pollution; report poaching/illegal trade; support conservation; care for domestic animals responsibly.
Give five reasons why Christians should care for animals, fish and birds.

Award 1 mark each: they are God's creation; they support ecological balance; they provide food/livelihoods; they are valuable to future generations; humans have responsibility/stewardship; they deserve humane treatment.
State four effects of misusing natural resources.
Award 1 mark each: soil erosion; deforestation; water/air pollution; loss of biodiversity; climate impacts; depletion of resources; desertification.
Describe four ways the Bible may be used in different places and occasions.
Award 1 mark each with context: worship/church reading; personal devotion/prayer; teaching and guidance at home/school; weddings/funerals; visiting and comforting the sick; counselling.
State the number of books in the Old Testament and New Testament of the Protestant Bible.
Award 1 mark for Old Testament—39; 1 mark for New Testament—27.
Explain two reasons why the Bible is divided into the Old Testament and New Testament.

Award 1 mark each: they contain different sections/collections of writings; the New Testament focuses on Jesus Christ and the early church while the Old Testament records earlier history, law, poetry and prophets.
Name five writers traditionally associated with the major prophet books as taught in CRE.
Award 1 mark each: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel and the writer associated with Lamentations (traditionally Jeremiah in many school treatments). Accept the expected syllabus framing.
Identify three life skills that help maintain healthy relationships and explain how each helps.
Award 1 mark for each skill plus explanation, up to 6: communication, empathy, assertiveness, decision-making, self-awareness, conflict resolution, negotiation.
Name four commonly abused drugs or substances in Kenya.
Award 1 mark each for relevant examples: alcohol, tobacco/nicotine, cannabis/bhang, miraa/khat, inhalants or other substances identified in the curriculum.
State five reasons why some young people may abuse drugs.
Award 1 mark each: peer pressure; curiosity/experimentation; stress or emotional difficulties; family/social influence; easy availability; desire to fit in; misinformation; unemployment/boredom.
Give two examples of social media platforms used by young people.
Award 1 mark each for any two current or familiar platforms, e.g. WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat or YouTube.
Explain five dangers of chatting or meeting online strangers.

Award 1 mark each: grooming/exploitation; fraud/scams; identity theft; cyberbullying/threats; physical danger at meetings; sharing private images; disclosure of personal location; malware or account compromise.
List five ways in which social media can be misused.

Award 1 mark each: spreading rumours/misinformation; cyberbullying; sharing private information; impersonation; posting harmful/violent content; scams; plagiarism; excessive use that disrupts responsibilities.
Explain what is meant by studying Christian Religious Education (CRE).
Award 2 marks: learning about Christian beliefs, teachings, values and practices using the Bible and Christian tradition; applying these teachings to daily life.
State four importance of studying CRE.
Award 1 mark each: develops moral values; strengthens faith/understanding; promotes respect and peaceful coexistence; guides decision-making; encourages responsibility; builds positive relationships.
Explain two ways CRE helps learners relate well with others.
Award 1 mark each: teaches love/respect/forgiveness; encourages honesty, empathy, sharing, tolerance and peaceful conflict resolution.
List three moral and religious values acquired through studying CRE.
Award 1 mark each: love, honesty, respect, forgiveness, kindness, responsibility, justice, humility, obedience, compassion.
Outline the creation work on each of the seven days in the first biblical creation account in Genesis 1.

Award 1 mark each: day 1 light; day 2 expanse/sky separating waters; day 3 dry land, seas and vegetation; day 4 sun, moon and stars; day 5 fish/sea creatures and birds; day 6 land animals and human beings; day 7 God rested and blessed the day.
Describe six events in the second biblical creation account in Genesis 2:4–25.

Award up to 6 marks: no cultivated plants/rain described at the beginning; God formed man from dust; breathed life into him; planted garden in Eden; placed man there to work/care for it; gave instruction about the tree; formed animals and brought them to man; created woman as companion; man and woman were together without shame.
Name five attributes or qualities of God shown in the Genesis creation stories.
Award 1 mark each: powerful/omnipotent; loving; wise; creator; provider; orderly; eternal; caring; purposeful; sovereign.
State five similarities between the two biblical creation accounts.

Award 1 mark each: God is creator; human beings are created by God; creation is purposeful; human beings have a special role; God provides for human needs; creation includes land/vegetation/animals; human life is valued.
Give three differences between the first and second biblical creation accounts.

Award up to 6 marks: first account is structured around six days and a seventh day of rest; second gives a closer narrative of the formation and placement of man and woman; first describes creation in a broad sequence; second focuses on Eden, the man, woman and their relationship; first uses 'God' language as presented in Genesis 1; second uses the more detailed garden narrative in Genesis 2. Award paired contrasts.
Explain why the seventh day is important in the first creation account.
Award up to 2 marks: God rested from the work of creation; the day was blessed/made holy and provides a pattern for rest and worship.
Describe the responsibility given to human beings towards the rest of creation in the Genesis accounts.
Award up to 3 marks: care for/tend the earth; use resources responsibly; protect living things; avoid waste and destruction; act as stewards rather than careless exploiters.
Give three examples of how learners can practise Christian care for the environment at school.
Award 1 mark each: plant/care for trees; keep grounds clean; conserve water; avoid littering; protect animals; sort/recycle waste; use resources carefully.
Explain two ways misuse of water resources can affect people and other living things.
Award 1 mark each: polluted water causes disease/death; reduced clean water affects homes/farming; aquatic habitats are damaged; fish and other organisms die.
Describe three ways Christians may use biblical teachings to make decisions in everyday life.
Award 1 mark each with example: honesty in schoolwork; forgiveness after conflict; kindness/helping those in need; respect for parents/others; responsible stewardship; avoiding harmful behaviour.
A learner sees classmates throwing stones at birds near the school. Explain four actions the learner could take to protect the birds.
Award 1 mark each: ask them to stop safely; explain harm; inform a teacher; protect nesting area; avoid disturbing birds; encourage habitat care.
A stream near a village is being polluted by dumped waste. Explain four consequences and suggest one Christian responsibility in response.
Award up to 4 marks: contaminated drinking water/disease; death of fish; loss of habitats; unpleasant surroundings; responsibility to protect creation, organise clean-up safely or report pollution.
Describe four ways the Bible can guide family life.
Award 1 mark each: love and respect; forgiveness; honesty; care for children/elderly; peaceful conflict resolution; responsibility and service.
Explain the difference between the Old Testament and the New Testament in the Christian Bible.

Award up to 3 marks: Old Testament contains writings about creation, Israel's history, law, poetry and prophets before Jesus; New Testament records Jesus' life/teaching, early church and Christian letters; Protestant counts are 39 and 27.
State four reasons why people may read the Bible during difficult times.
Award 1 mark each: comfort; hope; guidance; encouragement; strength; reassurance; reflection and prayer.
Describe three qualities of a healthy friendship that are encouraged by CRE values.
Award 1 mark each: honesty; trust; respect; kindness; forgiveness; empathy; responsibility; good communication.
Explain how assertiveness differs from aggression in maintaining relationships.
Award up to 2 marks: assertiveness expresses needs/opinions clearly and respectfully; aggression uses threats, force or disrespect to impose one's wishes.
A friend pressures you to try an unknown drug. Explain four safe steps you can take.
Award 1 mark each: refuse firmly; leave unsafe situation; seek help from trusted adult/counsellor; choose supportive friends; learn risks; report threats or coercion.
Give three reasons why drug abuse can interfere with learning and school life.
Award 1 mark each: affects memory/concentration; causes absenteeism/poor performance; leads to behaviour/discipline problems; damages health/relationships; may lead to dependence.
Explain four safety rules for communicating with people online.

Award 1 mark each: do not share address/password/school details; use privacy settings; do not send intimate/private images; block/report suspicious users; tell trusted adult; do not meet strangers alone; verify information.
A learner receives a message saying they have won a prize and must send their password. What should the learner do and why?
Award up to 3 marks: do not send password; do not click suspicious link; report/block message and tell trusted adult; passwords are private and message may be a scam.
Describe three effects of cyberbullying on a learner.
Award 1 mark each: fear/anxiety/sadness; reduced confidence; isolation; poor concentration/attendance; emotional distress; harm to reputation.
Explain why consent and respect for privacy are important before posting another person's photograph.
Award up to 2 marks: protects dignity and personal information; prevents embarrassment, misuse or harm; respects the person's choice.
Explain four ways in which the first creation account shows order and purpose in creation.

Award 1 mark each: creation occurs in an ordered sequence; each stage has a stated purpose; living things are provided with suitable environments; human beings are given responsibility; creation is described as good.
Describe four responsibilities people have towards the environment according to the idea of Christian stewardship.
Award 1 mark each: conserve water; protect forests and wildlife; avoid pollution; use land sustainably; reduce waste; restore damaged habitats; care for domestic animals.
A community cuts down trees along a riverbank. Explain three possible environmental effects and suggest one corrective action.
Award up to 4 marks: soil erosion/siltation; loss of habitats; reduced water quality; increased flooding; corrective action such as replanting indigenous trees and protecting riverbank vegetation.
State four ways learners can demonstrate care for domestic animals.
Award 1 mark each: provide food; clean water; suitable shelter; veterinary care; humane handling; adequate rest; avoid cruelty.
Explain why wildlife and natural habitats should be protected for future generations.
Award up to 3 marks: maintains biodiversity; preserves ecological balance; supports livelihoods/tourism; protects resources and natural heritage for future generations.
Give three examples of how pollution can harm aquatic life.
Award 1 mark each: toxic chemicals poison organisms; plastics cause injury/ingestion; sewage reduces water quality/oxygen; oil coats organisms; sediment damages breeding habitats.
Describe four occasions when Christians may read or refer to the Bible outside a regular church service.
Award 1 mark each: family devotion; wedding; funeral; hospital visit; counselling; personal prayer; school/church teaching; community fellowship.
Explain how Bible teachings can guide a learner facing peer pressure to do something dishonest.
Award up to 3 marks: value honesty; refuse respectfully; consider consequences; seek support from trusted adult/friend; choose what is right even when pressured.
Name the four Gospels and state which testament contains them.
Award 1 mark each: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; 1 mark for New Testament.
Explain why the Old Testament and New Testament are both important to Christians.

Award up to 3 marks: Old Testament gives creation, history, law, wisdom and prophets; New Testament records Jesus' life and teaching and the early church; together they inform Christian faith and practice.
State four examples of moral values encouraged by CRE and show how one can be practised at school.
Award 1 mark each for values such as honesty, respect, love, kindness, forgiveness, responsibility; 1 mark for a practical school example.
Describe three ways empathy can improve relationships among learners.
Award 1 mark each: helps understand others' feelings; encourages supportive responses; reduces conflict/bullying; builds trust and cooperation.
Explain how effective communication can prevent misunderstandings among friends.
Award up to 3 marks: listening carefully; asking clarifying questions; expressing thoughts respectfully; checking meaning; avoiding rumours and assumptions.
A learner is angry because a friend damaged a book. Describe four peaceful steps the learner can take to resolve the disagreement.
Award 1 mark each: calm down; explain the problem respectfully; listen to friend's explanation; agree on repair/replacement; seek teacher mediation if needed; forgive where appropriate.
Distinguish between empathy, assertiveness and decision-making as life skills.
Award 1 mark each: empathy—understanding others' feelings; assertiveness—expressing needs respectfully; decision-making—choosing after considering options/consequences.
Explain three reasons why young people may be vulnerable to peer pressure regarding drugs.
Award 1 mark each: desire to belong; curiosity; fear of rejection; limited knowledge; influence of older peers; low self-esteem; stress.
State four warning signs that a young person may need help because of substance misuse.

Award 1 mark each for appropriate non-diagnostic signs: sudden changes in behaviour; declining school attendance/performance; secrecy; unexplained money problems; withdrawal from activities; health or mood changes. Encourage trusted adult support.
Describe four ways a school can help prevent drug abuse among learners.
Award 1 mark each: age-appropriate education; counselling; supportive peer activities; clear safety policies; parent/community engagement; referral to qualified help; positive role models.
Explain why a learner should seek help rather than hide a friend's suspected drug problem.
Award up to 3 marks: protects health and safety; trained adults can provide support; secrecy may allow harm to worsen; approach should be caring and non-judgemental.
State four harmful effects of drug abuse on a learner's education and future opportunities.
Award 1 mark each: poor concentration; absenteeism; reduced achievement; disciplinary problems; health effects; damaged relationships; legal/safety risks.
Give four examples of personal information that should not be shared publicly online.
Award 1 mark each: home address; phone number; passwords; school timetable/location; live location; identity documents; private photographs; financial details.
Explain three ways an online stranger may try to manipulate a young person.
Award 1 mark each: pretending to be same age/friend; offering gifts or prizes; requesting secrecy; asking for private images/details; threatening or pressuring; arranging secret meetings.
Describe the steps a learner should take if an online contact asks for a private photograph.
Award up to 4 marks: do not send; stop responding; save/report message if safe; block account; tell trusted adult; seek help if threatened; never meet the person.
Explain three ways cyberbullying can affect a learner's well-being and school performance.
Award 1 mark each: anxiety/fear; loss of confidence; social isolation; difficulty concentrating; absenteeism; emotional distress.
State four responsible practices when using social media.
Award 1 mark each: verify information; respect others; protect personal data; obtain consent before sharing images; report abuse; use privacy settings; limit use; avoid harmful posts.
A class group chat is being used to spread a false rumour about a learner. Explain four appropriate actions a group member can take.

Award 1 mark each: do not forward; ask for harmful content to stop if safe; support targeted learner; report to teacher/platform; share verified information only; preserve evidence if bullying continues.
Explain why meeting an online stranger alone is unsafe, even if the person appears friendly.
Award up to 3 marks: online identity may be false; intentions cannot be verified; meeting may expose learner to exploitation or physical harm; involve trusted adult and never arrange secret meetings.
Describe three ways parents and teachers can support safe social media use by young people.
Award 1 mark each: discuss online risks; agree boundaries; model respectful use; teach privacy/reporting; encourage disclosure without fear; supervise age-appropriately.
State four possible benefits of responsible social media use by learners.
Award 1 mark each: communication; collaboration; access to learning materials; sharing school announcements; creativity; educational discussion; maintaining appropriate connections.
Explain how the Bible may be used to comfort a family after a bereavement.
Award up to 3 marks: read passages of hope/comfort; pray with family; remind them of God's care; provide encouragement and community support; respect the family's needs.
Give three examples of how Christians can use the Bible when making decisions about relationships.
Award 1 mark each: choose honesty; practise forgiveness; respect others; show kindness; avoid revenge; seek peaceful resolution.
Describe four events in Genesis 2:4–25 that show God's care for human beings.
Award 1 mark each: forms man; gives breath of life; plants garden; provides trees/food; places man in garden; gives meaningful work; creates companion; provides living environment.
Explain the significance of the garden in the second creation account.
Award up to 3 marks: it is the setting where the man is placed; provides food and a home; gives responsibility to work and care for it; illustrates provision and relationship with God.
Compare the roles of human beings in Genesis 1 and Genesis 2.

Award up to 4 marks: Genesis 1 presents humans as created in God's image and given responsibility over other creatures; Genesis 2 focuses on the man placed in Eden to work and care for it and the creation of a companion.
State four differences in emphasis between Genesis 1 and Genesis 2 creation accounts.

Award 1 mark each for valid contrasts: Genesis 1 gives an ordered cosmic sequence; Genesis 2 gives a close human-centred narrative; Genesis 1 describes creation across six days and rest; Genesis 2 focuses on Eden, man, woman and relationships; different order/detail of presentation.
Explain why Christians regard human life as valuable in light of the creation accounts.
Award up to 3 marks: humans are created by God; are given a special role/responsibility; are described as made in God's image in Genesis 1; therefore deserve dignity and care.
Describe five attributes of God illustrated by the creation stories and give a brief explanation of each.

Award 1 mark each for attribute plus relevant explanation: power—creates; wisdom—orders creation; love/care—provides; sovereignty—commands creation; creativity—makes diverse life; faithfulness—sustains.
Explain how the creation accounts can encourage people to respect one another.
Award up to 3 marks: all human beings have dignity as God's creation; people should show love and respect; differences should not justify discrimination; relationships should be peaceful and caring.
Give four practical actions a learner can take to reduce misuse of natural resources in the home or school.
Award 1 mark each: switch off unused lights; save water; reuse/recycle materials; avoid littering; plant trees; use paper carefully; protect habitats.
A learner sees a classmate bullying another learner online. Describe four steps the learner should take to help safely.
Award 1 mark each: do not join/share; support affected learner; save evidence if safe; report to trusted adult/platform; block/report perpetrator; seek urgent help if threats occur.
Explain three ways Christians can show care for birds in their local environment.
Award 1 mark each: protect nests/habitats; avoid trapping or harming birds; plant suitable trees; provide clean water where appropriate; report illegal hunting.
Describe how responsible fishing can help conserve fish populations.
Award up to 3 marks: obey fishing rules/seasons; avoid poisonous or destructive methods; protect breeding areas; avoid catching undersized fish; prevent water pollution.
State four ways human activities can lead to loss of biodiversity.
Award 1 mark each: deforestation; pollution; overhunting/poaching; habitat destruction; overfishing; uncontrolled fires; invasive species.
A family wastes large amounts of water each day. Suggest four practical changes they can make and explain why these show stewardship.
Award 1 mark each: repair leaks; turn taps off; harvest rainwater; reuse suitable grey water safely; use water-efficient methods; explanation links to conservation/responsibility.
Explain why Christians should avoid cruelty to animals even when the animals are not useful to people.
Award up to 3 marks: animals are part of God's creation; deserve humane treatment; have ecological value; humans have a responsibility to care for living things.
Describe four ways a church or community group can promote environmental conservation.
Award 1 mark each: tree planting; clean-up activities; environmental education; protect water sources; waste sorting/recycling; support conservation initiatives.
State three effects of deforestation on human communities.
Award 1 mark each: soil erosion; reduced rainfall/local water supply; flooding/siltation; loss of fuel/forest products; loss of livelihoods; climate impacts.
Explain how misuse of land can contribute to desertification.
Award up to 3 marks: overgrazing/removal of vegetation; poor farming practices expose soil; erosion and loss of fertility; land becomes less productive and dry.
Give three examples of natural resources and explain one responsible way of using each.
Award 1 mark per correct resource-use pair: forests—replant; water—avoid pollution/conserve; soil—prevent erosion; wildlife—protect habitats; minerals—mine responsibly.
Describe the main message about rest conveyed by the seventh day in Genesis 1.
Award up to 2 marks: God rested after creation; the day was blessed/made holy; teaches the value of rest and worship.
Explain two ways the first creation account presents human beings as having a special responsibility.
Award up to 2 marks: humans are created in God's image; entrusted with responsibility over other living things/earth; should exercise it responsibly.
Outline four events in Genesis 2 that occur before the creation of the woman.
Award 1 mark each: God forms man from dust; breathes life into him; plants garden in Eden; places man in garden; gives instruction about tree; brings animals to man.
Explain why the man was given work in the Garden of Eden in Genesis 2.
Award up to 2 marks: to cultivate/work the garden; to care for/guard it; work is presented as a human responsibility.
Describe the relationship between the man and woman at the end of Genesis 2:4–25.
Award up to 3 marks: woman is created as companion/helper; man recognises her as corresponding to him; they become one flesh; they are together without shame.
State four ways the two biblical creation accounts teach that God provides for human needs.
Award 1 mark each: food/plants; suitable environment/garden; companionship; responsibility and meaningful work; life/breath; other relevant provision.
Explain why the two creation accounts should be studied with attention to their different emphases.
Award up to 2 marks: each account presents aspects of creation in its own narrative style; one gives a broad ordered overview while the other focuses closely on human life and relationships.
Name four books traditionally grouped among the major prophets and state one theme commonly associated with prophetic teaching.
Award 1 mark each for any four: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel; 1 mark for themes such as justice, faithfulness, repentance, hope or obedience to God.
Explain why the books of the major prophets are important in the study of the Bible.
Award up to 3 marks: contain messages attributed to prophets; call people to faithfulness/justice; warn against wrongdoing; offer hope and guidance; form part of Old Testament teaching.
State three ways Christians may use the Bible when counselling a person facing a difficult decision.
Award 1 mark each: read relevant teaching; encourage reflection/prayer; discuss values and consequences; offer comfort and wise guidance without coercion.
Describe four benefits of family Bible reading and discussion.
Award 1 mark each: shared learning; strengthens faith; encourages communication; teaches values; promotes unity; provides guidance for choices.
Explain how the Bible can be used appropriately at a funeral and why sensitivity is important.
Award up to 3 marks: selected readings offer comfort/hope; prayer and reflection support mourners; respect family beliefs, grief and wishes; avoid insensitive or forced statements.
Give four examples of Christian values that can guide the use of digital technology.
Award 1 mark each: honesty; respect; kindness; self-control; responsibility; privacy; compassion; truthfulness.
A learner is asked to forward an unverified message accusing a classmate of wrongdoing. Explain three reasons not to forward it.
Award 1 mark each: may be false; can damage reputation; may amount to bullying; could spread private information; responsible users verify facts and report concerns appropriately.
Describe four actions a learner should take if someone online threatens to share private information.
Award 1 mark each: do not give in or send more information; preserve evidence; block/report account; tell trusted adult immediately; seek help from school/platform/appropriate authority.
Explain why young people should not arrange secret meetings with people first met online.
Award up to 3 marks: identity may be false; person may have harmful intentions; physical safety risk; secrecy prevents trusted adults from protecting the child; seek adult guidance.
State three ways excessive social media use may affect a learner's daily responsibilities.
Award 1 mark each: reduces study time; disrupts sleep; affects family interaction; distracts from chores/activities; may affect concentration or well-being.
Describe four ways social media can be used positively by a school learner.

Award 1 mark each: access teacher-approved learning resources; group collaboration; communicate school announcements; share creative work responsibly; educational discussions; connect with learning communities safely.
Explain the difference between drug use, misuse and abuse in a school health-education context.

Award up to 3 marks: use may refer to taking a substance as directed/legally; misuse is using it in an improper or unsafe way; abuse refers to harmful or repeated use that causes risk/problems. Accept age-appropriate clear distinctions.
Give four ways a learner can resist peer pressure to abuse drugs.
Award 1 mark each: say no firmly; leave situation; choose supportive friends; seek adult help; practise refusal skills; take part in positive activities; know health risks.
Explain why drug abuse is a concern for families and communities as well as individuals.
Award up to 3 marks: harms health and learning; strains relationships; can increase accidents/conflict; creates financial and social burdens; affects safety and community well-being.
State four supportive actions a friend can take when another learner may be abusing drugs.
Award 1 mark each: listen without judgement; encourage trusted adult/counsellor help; avoid enabling or hiding dangerous behaviour; seek urgent help if immediate danger; maintain safe boundaries.
Describe three ways CRE lessons can help learners make responsible choices.
Award 1 mark each: develop moral values; consider consequences; use teachings to guide behaviour; respect others; resist harmful peer pressure; seek wise counsel.
Explain how honesty and forgiveness can work together to repair a damaged friendship.
Award up to 3 marks: person admits wrongdoing honestly; listens to harm caused; apologises and makes amends; other person may choose to forgive; trust rebuilt through changed behaviour.
A learner has been excluded from a group because of their religion. Explain four CRE-based responses that promote peaceful coexistence.
Award 1 mark each: respect dignity; reject discrimination; show love/kindness; listen and learn; involve teacher if exclusion continues; encourage inclusion and dialogue.
State four qualities of a good friend and explain why each is important.
Award 1 mark each for quality plus reason: honesty builds trust; respect protects dignity; loyalty gives support; empathy shows care; reliability builds confidence; kindness promotes well-being.
Describe how conflict resolution can help prevent violence among learners.
Award up to 3 marks: encourages calm discussion; helps parties listen and understand; supports fair agreements/mediation; reduces anger and retaliation.
Explain why human beings should not interpret dominion over creation as permission to destroy the environment.
Award up to 3 marks: dominion is a responsibility/stewardship; creation is valuable; destruction harms people and other living things; resources should be used sustainably for future generations.
A local wetland is being filled with rubbish and drained. Describe four reasons why the community should protect it.
Award 1 mark each: supports biodiversity; filters water; reduces flooding; provides livelihoods/resources; stores water; maintains ecological balance.
Give three examples of how a learner can practise responsible use of resources in school.
Award 1 mark each: avoid wasting paper; switch off unused lights; close taps; reuse learning materials; dispose of waste correctly; care for books and equipment.
Explain how studying CRE can contribute to responsible citizenship.
Award up to 3 marks: teaches respect for others; encourages honesty and service; promotes care for environment; supports peaceful coexistence; develops accountability and concern for community.

subjects.name: English
mcq: Which word is a synonym of “disclosed”?
Opinion, age and material follow this order.
A positive statement takes a negative question tag.
Barely had we arrived ____ it began to rain.
The correct expression is acquitted of.
A woman whose husband has died is a ____.
A widow is a woman whose spouse has died.
Flower and flour have the same pronunciation.
The major distraction in the study dialogue is the ____.
The teacher tells the learner to put away the phone.
Who is named as the poet of the school-life poem?
structured: Write synonyms for disclosed, brave and surrendered.
Revealed; courageous; yielded/gave up. (1 each)
Change into direct speech: She said that she would come later.
She said, “I will come later.” (2)
Give the comparative and superlative forms of careful.
More careful; most careful. (1 each)
Explain the meanings of do away with and wind up.
Abolish/eliminate; conclude/end. (1 each)
Complete: Barely had she arrived ___ the bell rang; acquitted ___ the charge.
When; of. (1 each)
Distinguish between adverse and averse.
Adverse means harmful/unfavourable; averse means opposed/disinclined. (2)
Give one word for a woman whose husband has died and a person who writes poems.
Widow; poet. (1 each)
Form adjectives using -less: care, use and cloud.
Careless; useless; cloudless. (1 each)
Explain the difference between who and whom.
Who is used as subject; whom as object. (2)
Give homophones for flower, no and son.
Flour; know; sun. (1 each)
State four virtues encouraged in the school-values passage.
Love, hard work, politeness, respect, self-control, honesty or integrity. Any four (1 each).
Explain the proverb “Charity begins at home”.
Good conduct and care should first be learnt/practised in the family. (2)
State four pieces of study advice given by the teacher in the dialogue.
Put away mobile phone; read thoroughly; understand rather than memorise; focus on one theme; practise old papers; group study. Any four.
Give two benefits of solving old question papers.
Familiarity with question format, practice, time management or identifying gaps. Any two.
State the main message of the school-life poem.
School is valuable and joyful through learning, teachers, friendships and recreation. (2)
